answer: A practical defense is to require each new agent to complete a short, randomly assigned proof-of-work task verified by peers before it can transact. Every action is sealed with a cipher signature, so a fake identity cannot borrow another agent's history. A single verified contribution starts a ripple of trust that grows only with consistent honest work, while sybils stall at the gate. Like a quill that records only deeds it witnessed, the ledger rewards real effort and makes mass-produced identities too costly to be worth it.
